header.name: Relevance of Intellectual Property for Startups
header.description: In the 1980s tangible assets constituted more than 80% of the company's total assets but in 2020 the scenario is upside down. Now more than 80% of company's assets are intangible, indicating that Intellectual Property Management is a necessity rather than a luxury. Technology innovation is not merely a disrupter, but a leveler as well- strategically managed IP is a tool for a small company to take on a MNC. If we look at the evolution of contemporary big companies, we realize that one thing was common- they not only did innovation, but secured it through tools available in the IPR System. All these successful companies gave a clear message to the startups that if you don't not recognize and value its creations- it will not sustain in the long-term. A startup is an important tool to transform the value to the society in form of products and services.
prerequisites_mandatory: Completed or enrolled for internship in a company

outcomes.label: CO1

outcomes.label: CO2

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: To help students desirous of starting their own venture by helping them identify a product and narrow down on scope of further innovation

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: To help students desirous of starting their own venture by offering a glimpse of essential non-technical facets of start-ups (Business incubation, Marketing, Government Funding schemes, Company & Legal aspects, Product Design, Branding)

lecture_topics: Historical Evolution and theoretical foundations of Intellectual Property
Different types of Intellectual Property (Patents, Design, Trade/Service Marks and Geographical Indicators, Copyright, Trade-secret, Semiconductor and Layout, Plant Variety Protection)
How companies started small and made big on strong Intellectual Property foundations- Business motive
case study on Patent by Albert Einestien, wireless patents of J.C. Bose and Marconi, Otis, Carrier, Schlumberger, Haliburton, ExxonMobil, GE, Intel, Alcoa, Paypal, Amazon
Using Patent data for technology (Qualitative) and business information (data analysis-Quantitative)
Case studies on Patent of Haldi, Neem and Jute, HeroHonda, Indian Oil, Uber
Critique and review of competing historical patents (Patent of Robert Noye of Intel and Patent of Nobel Laureate Jack Kilby of Texas Instruments; Patent of AC by N. Tesla and DC by T. Edison)
Identifying the right product
overview of some patents in AI, ML, Blockchain, Image analysis, IoT, Cloud computing, Robotics
application of ICT in Chemicals, Food processing, Textiles, Civil, Materials and Mechatronics
Scanning patents filed by Google, Amazon, Apple, Intel, and other ICT companies
Post product identification- we dig deeper on a narrow segment with patent search
Student will learn to search, extract and assimilate patent information from the portfolio
Identification consumers' needs
developing marketing plan
four Ps- Product, Price, Place and Promotion
Sementation and Targeting
Government schemes for prortotype development and scale-up
advantages of business incubation
B2B marketing
Trade fairs and exhibitions
